headline: I Tried to Mediate My Kids' Argument Over the TV Remote by Invoking Trilateral Diplomacy
body:
When my seven-year-old demanded control over the Cartoon Network remote, I realized my household was essentially a geopolitical hotspot. To restore order, I sat both of them down at the dining table and insisted that we treat the remote as a high-stakes resource, noting that my neighbor’s dog barking in the yard was clearly an act of 'third-party influence' aimed at destabilizing our snack budget.

I told my children that I had personally briefed our family cat on the importance of maintaining regional parity, even though she spent the entire negotiation staring at a dust bunny. My spouse suggested we just buy a second remote, but I dismissed that as a naive 'binary solution' that failed to address the complex underlying power dynamics of who gets to hold the device during the transition between shows.

By lunchtime, we had drafted a six-page memorandum of understanding regarding volume levels and channel surfing quotas, though the youngest eventually breached the treaty by switching to a nature documentary. I am now considering imposing economic sanctions on their access to the iPad to ensure that the delicate balance of domestic power remains firmly under my control.
caption: I watched the news about global envoys and realized I could do that too. It's all about posturing until someone cries. #ParentingTips #Diplomacy #TrilateralTalks (satire)
igHook: Ever felt like your own living room is a war zone needing a peace treaty?
